page: Vultr vbm-8c-128gb-amd is a bare metal server featuring a dedicated AMD EPYC 4345P processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The CPU provides 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz, supported by 32 MB of L3 cache. The hardware configuration includes 123.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, yielding approximately 7.71 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with 3890 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, and the system includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core metrics and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 operations placing in the top 10% of tested servers. Memory performance is mixed; while the PassMark memory score ranks in the top 10%, large-block uncached write memory bandwidth is weak, falling into the bottom 25% at 21.85 GB/sec. Multi-core performance, database operations, and static web serving throughput align with average mid-tier expectations. For machine learning workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier text generation speeds for small 135M models, though performance scales down to average levels when processing medium 7B models.

From a resource density perspective, this bare metal server offers a high ratio of dedicated physical CPU cores, DDR5 memory, and local NVMe storage. The combination of high single-core CPU speeds and substantial local storage capacity makes it suitable for database hosting, memory-intensive applications, and localized file processing. However, the lower multi-core scaling and weak large-block write bandwidth represent key tradeoffs for highly parallelized write-heavy workloads. Appropriate use cases include relational databases, caching layers, and web serving applications that benefit from dedicated hardware isolation.
